description:
Local memory and context for you and your AI agent: Markdown notes, documents and tasks on your disk, with an MCP server for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

Tisty keeps what you know on your own machine: notes, documents and tasks, in plain
Markdown files you can read without it. Everything you do is written to an append-only
log, so nothing is lost by accident and a change can be walked back; erasing something
for good is the one step that cannot. No account, no
subscription, no telemetry, no server. Sync, if you want it, goes through a folder both
your machines already reach, and an assistant can come in through a door you open.
Tisty 1.46.0
Languages others add wait for your review, and your AI agent remembers for less
- When someone who edits your shared document adds a language, it waits as a proposal until you keep it or leave it out, and readers only see what you kept.
- You review a language as Folio holds it, with who added it, its words and its pictures.
- If a language you kept changes, its row says so and shows the new version against the one you approved.
- What you left out stays aside, to review again whenever you like.
- Readers see who translated and who reviewed each language someone else added.
- Changing the edit link, or translating under someone else's, tells you first what will happen to those languages.
- The day's counts open over all your lists and stop at +99, and each list has a menu of its own.
- A document in many languages shows only the one you read and how many it has.
- Connecting Tisty to your AI assistant costs a third less.
- In assistants that show them, such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot in VS Code, commands pick up where you left off, plan a task, look up how something was solved or keep a decision, and your documents can be mentioned with @.
- The help and the guide tell how your agent picks up where it left off and keeps what it learns.
